Thanks,

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: Intel MKL libraries with remote StatET connection crashes R?
messages.subject_clean: Intel MKL libraries with remote StatET connection crashes R?
messages.body_plain:
Keith Woolner <keith@...> writes:

> 
> Is anyone using the Intel MKL math libraries with StatET connecting to a 
> remote R server?
> 
> I am trying to connect to R 2.15.3 running on Linux from a Windows box 
> running Eclipse 3.8.2 and StatET (Java Core 1.1.3, Eclient 1.2.1).  Have 
> been using this setup for months without issue.  We recently recompiled 
> R with the Intel MKL optimized numeric libraries, and are running into 
> problems, but only through StatET.
> 
> If I run a simple matrix operation like "crossprod(1:4)" in a local R 
> session on the server, it returns fine.  On a more complex operation, it 
> is noticeably faster (one test went from 86 seconds down to 35 seconds), 
> which is what we were hoping to see by using these libraries.
> 
> But if I start a remote session via Eclipse/StatET, and run the same 
> command, it kills the entire remote R session.  In the log files on the 
> server I see the error"Intel MKL FATAL ERROR: Cannot load libmkl_mc3.so 
> or libmkl_def.so".  I've compared LD_LIBRARY_PATH in both the local and 
> remote sessions, and can't find any differences -- both have entries 
> pointing to the Intel MKL directories.
> 
> I've fiddled with numerous settings and environment variables, tried 
> reinstalling rj and rj.gd, without success.  I don't know if this is a 
> StatET problem, an Intel MKL problem, or a local configuration problem, 
> but since it works when run locally without StatET involved, I wanted to 
> ask the list whether anyone else has this kind of configuration working?
> 
> Any suggestions would be appreciated.
> 
> Thanks,
> Keith
> 
> 

Hi,

I have a similar problem with R 3.0.2 compiled against Intel MKL 11.1's 
version of BLAS/LAPACK. However, I run Eclipse 4.3.1/StatET 3.3 directly on 
the cluster, not via the remote session. So if I run R from the console, 
everything works fine. But in StatET console any command that uses Intel's 
BLAS, e.g. "1 %*% 1" results in session termination. I had not noticed any 
differences in Sys.getenv() if run either from shell or StatET (actually, 
I've also tried different combinations of StatET/rj/rj.gd without any luck).

It would be great if Stephan/StatET Team could provide any feedback on the 
issue.

With Best Regards,
  Alexey

enabling shared R-BLAS library. I suspect that just static linking would be 
enough. So now "1 %*% 1" doesn't crash StatET.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Brandon,

[2014-01-10 18:56] brandon willard wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I was just adding roxygen text in StatET when I noticed that hitting
> enter doesn't add a comment token (i.e. #') to the new line.  Is there
> an option I'm missing?  It would be great if it behaved like Java /**/
> comments.

StatET adds #' to new lines, if you are not in the last line of the 
Roxygen comment. In contrast to Java, Roxygen comments doesn't have a 
special token for the end (*/).

>
> Also, is there a bug/issue/request tracking system for StatET?  I didn't
> see it enabled on the Github page.

No, at moment there is not issue tracker for StatET.

messages.subject: Evaluating StatET against RStudio
messages.body_plain:
Because I was having a slight issue (since resolved) in StatET figuring 
out how to set up quick invocation of the View function on the object 
browser, I decided to try the latest version of RStudio again as an 
alternative.

So I installed RStudio 0.98 and used it for a couple of days.  In the 
end, I could not stand it any more and switched back to StatET in a hurry.

The RStudio fonts are poor in my opinion. At first, they were totally 
hollowed out on Windows 7 with 16-bit colors.   I got around the 
hollowing out by switching to 32 bit colors, but no matter how I set the 
fonts, I could not get a satisfactory overall display layout.

Actually, the whole user interface of RStudio gives the feeling of being 
text based rather than a true GUI.  It is not as responsive or flexible 
as StatET under Eclipse.  There are nowhere near as many customizations 
available as with StatET.   I found it awkward and limiting.

A real killer for me was the lack of value popup display when you hover 
the mouse cursor over a variable name.  I also found the debugger user 
interface crude in comparison.

On the other hand, there are some advantages in RStudio. You can set it 
to source in every time you do a save.  In general, I found executing 
more intuitive than under StatET.  There are a lot fewer options to 
configure and menus to navigate.  Everything works as expected right 
from the start.  The availability of View inside the IDE is nice.  (The 
StatET DataViewer is nice too and has additional sort capabilities but 
lacks full support of IDates and some other types).

I think it is great that RStudio is available and is readily usable by 
newcomers without the learning curve that Eclipse takes.

I know that quite a few people love it and in fact have said they 
preferred it to Eclipse/StatET.

But in my opinion, one cannot achieve the usability and productivity 
with RStudio that you can with StatET, even though StatET has a learning 
curve for those unfamiliar with Eclipse.
